title: Tapping on the window
brief: You're Tomás, and the café isn't open yet. An older gentleman is knocking on the glass for his morning tinto, closed or not. He's a regular and he's older than you, so use usted. Find out who he is and send him off happy.

turns.npc: ¡Buenos días! ¿Hay tinto o no hay tinto?
turns.npcEn: Morning! Is there coffee or isn't there?
turns.intent: Greet him politely and tell him yes, there's coffee.
accept: Buenos días, señor. Sí, hay tinto.
Buenos días. Sí, señor, hay tinto.
Hola, buenos días. Sí, hay tinto.

turns.npc: Soy Hernando, cliente de Rosa. ¿Usted es el mesero?
turns.npcEn: I'm Hernando, one of Rosa's customers. Are you the waiter?
turns.intent: Tell him no, you're not the waiter: you're Tomás, from Toronto.
accept: No, no soy el mesero. Soy Tomás, de Toronto.
No, señor. Soy Tomás y soy de Toronto.
No, me llamo Tomás. Soy de Toronto.

turns.npc: ¿De Toronto? ¡Un canadiense en el café de Rosa! Mucho gusto.
turns.npcEn: From Toronto? A Canadian in Rosa's café! Nice to meet you.
turns.intent: Say it's nice to meet him too, and ask him if he's from Bogotá. Remember: usted.
accept: Mucho gusto, señor Hernando. ¿Usted es de Bogotá?
Con mucho gusto. ¿Usted es de Bogotá?

turns.npc: ¡Claro que sí! Soy de La Candelaria. Bueno, un tinto, por favor.
turns.npcEn: Of course! I'm from La Candelaria. Right then, a coffee, please.
turns.intent: Say of course, and offer him a bread roll as well.
accept: Claro que sí, señor. ¿Un tinto y un pan?

turns.npcEn: Bread? Vale's bread? I love it! How much is it?
turns.intent: Tell him it's on you: you're giving him the coffee and the bread (use regalar).
accept: Regalo el tinto y el pan, señor.
No, señor. Regalo el tinto y el pan.

turns.npcEn: Thank you, Tomás! See you tomorrow, then?
accept: De nada, señor. Chao, nos vemos.
Con mucho gusto. Nos vemos, señor.
